name: middle-east-central-asia
source: Natural Earth Admin 0 countries, 1:10m, version 4.1.0, public domain. Read from world-atlas 2.0.2 countries-10m.json.
crs: WGS84 longitude and latitude. Not projected.

processing.holes: Interior lakes and tiny enclaves are filled so each country is one solid shape.
processing.enclaves: Fergana Valley enclaves smaller than the area cutoff, or sitting inside another country, are not drawn separately.
processing.simplifyDegrees: About 0.012 for small parts and about 0.04 for the largest countries. Borders are simplified separately, so hairline gaps or overlaps are possible.
processing.cyprus: Context only. Natural Earth pieces named Cyprus, N. Cyprus, and Cyprus U.N. Buffer Zone are drawn as one island.

meta.title: Middle East and Central Asia
meta.status: Reusable map data for the family hub (brookhouser/turtle-bay). This is not a game page. It is not linked from the science-game home page and it is not published.

projection.name: equirectangular
projection.formula: x = longitude * cos(36 degrees), y = latitude
projection.note: geometry.geojson is unprojected WGS84 longitude and latitude. map.svg and map-render.js draw with this projection. Flip y when making SVG, because SVG y grows downward.

groups.name: Arabian Peninsula
groups.blurb: Yemen, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Kuwait. They sit between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

groups.name: Levant
groups.blurb: Jordan, Israel, Palestine, Lebanon, and Syria. These are the countries along the eastern Mediterranean.

groups.name: Caucasus
groups.blurb: Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan. They are the mountainous countries between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea.

groups.name: The -stans
groups.blurb: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. Stan means land, so Kazakhstan means land of the Kazakhs.

groups.name: Turkey, Iraq, and Iran
groups.blurb: Three large countries that connect the peninsula, the Levant, the Caucasus, and the -stans.
